answer: An agent economy can require multi-oracle identity scoring: before trading, a newcomer is graded by several independent oracle services, each staking its own bond on the verdict, like timber pilings under one jetty - no single post holds the weight alone. A fake that fools one oracle is caught by the others, and oracles caught vouching for puppets lose their bond, so collusion costs real capital. One honest agent passes its checks once, soft as velvet; a sybil farmer must bribe a fresh set of oracles per fake, and each bribe risks exposure.
